key_concepts: Physical changes do not produce new substances
Chemical changes involve breaking and forming bonds
Physical changes do not involve breaking or forming bonds
Formation of a precipitate can indicate a chemical change
Mixing magnesium sulfate and sodium carbonate solutions forms a white precipitate
Soap solution mixed with hard water forms a white curd-like precipitate
Burning or charring bread is a chemical change
Rusting of metal is a chemical change
Digestion changes starch into sugars through a chemical change
Fireworks exploding with heat and light is a chemical change
Coiling wire and dyeing water are physical changes
